name: Donepezil
uses: Mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease; improves memory, attention and daily functioning.
warnings: Take at bedtime. Report fainting, very slow pulse or stomach bleeding. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Memantine
warnings: Dose is increased gradually over weeks. Tell the doctor about kidney problems.

name: Rivastigmine
uses: Mild to moderate Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease dementia.
warnings: Apply patch to clean, dry skin and rotate sites. Remove old patch before applying a new one.

name: Galantamine
warnings: Take with food. Report severe skin reactions.

name: Metformin
warnings: Stop and seek help for unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing or severe tiredness (lactic acidosis). Tell the doctor before contrast scans.

name: Amlodipine
warnings: Rise slowly from sitting to avoid dizziness.

name: Losartan
uses: High blood pressure; kidney protection in diabetes.
warnings: Not for use in pregnancy. Avoid potassium supplements unless advised.

name: Aspirin
uses: Low dose: prevention of heart attack and stroke. Higher dose: pain and fever.
warnings: Take after food. Report black stools or vomiting blood.

name: Atorvastatin
uses: Lowers cholesterol; reduces heart attack and stroke risk.
warnings: Report unexplained muscle pain or dark urine.
foodAdvice: Any time of day, usually evening.

name: Simvastatin
warnings: Take at night. Report muscle pain or weakness.

name: Warfarin
uses: Prevents blood clots (atrial fibrillation, DVT, heart valves).
warnings: Regular INR blood tests are essential. Keep vitamin K intake (green vegetables) steady.
foodAdvice: Same time each day; consistent diet.

name: Clopidogrel
uses: Prevents clots after heart attack, stroke or stent.
warnings: Do not stop without talking to the doctor, especially after a stent.

name: Omeprazole
uses: Acid reflux, stomach ulcers, stomach protection.
warnings: Long-term use may affect bone strength and B12 levels.

name: Levothyroxine
warnings: Take on an empty stomach, 30–60 minutes before breakfast, away from calcium and iron.

name: Furosemide
uses: Fluid retention from heart failure, kidney or liver disease.
warnings: Take in the morning. Report muscle cramps or extreme thirst.

name: Sertraline
uses: Depression and anxiety, common alongside dementia.
warnings: Takes 2–4 weeks to work. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Quetiapine
uses: Severe agitation or psychosis; used cautiously in dementia.
warnings: Increased risk of stroke and death in elderly dementia patients — only under specialist supervision.

name: Paracetamol
warnings: Never exceed 4g in 24 hours. Check other medicines for hidden paracetamol.

name: Ibuprofen
warnings: Avoid in heart failure, kidney disease or with blood thinners unless advised.

name: Vitamin D3
sideEffects: Rare; high doses can raise calcium
warnings: Do not exceed the prescribed dose.

name: Vitamin B12
uses: B12 deficiency, nerve and blood health; often low on metformin.
warnings: None significant.

name: Digoxin
warnings: Narrow safety margin — never double a missed dose. Report nausea or yellow vision.

name: Insulin
warnings: Always keep a sugar source nearby. Rotate injection sites.
foodAdvice: Timing depends on the insulin type — follow the plan exactly.

name: Lorazepam
warnings: High fall and confusion risk in older adults; short courses only.

name: Melatonin
warnings: Take 1–2 hours before bedtime.
